messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.inference>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>
Date: Mon, 1 Jun 2026 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API unit-economics exercise and traffic sanity check

Hi Ethan — thanks again for the demo today. Quick recap and a short ask so we can put together a tailored pricing sketch and a mutual action plan.

Summary of what I heard on the call:
- Product: interactive summarization + user Q&A over user-uploaded documents (mostly PDF/markdown).
- Expected active users for next 12mo: 45k monthly active; peak usage tied to business hours in US.
- Current ML footprint: prototype on single GPU with lots of cold-cache latency spikes.

What we need to finalize to produce a hosted-API proposal: (if you can confirm the bullets below, we’ll run a quick unit-econ exercise and send a 2-option price band)

1) Expected monthly token consumption (approx):
   - Best guess for month 1 (pilot): 5–10M tokens
   - Target steady-state month: 60–90M tokens/month
2) Average prompt + response token mix:
   - Avg input tokens: ~80
   - Avg generated tokens: ~220
   - (If you expect longer outputs on summaries, call that out)
3) Peak concurrency / TPS characteristics:
   - 99th percentile API TPS during peak hour: ? (we usually see customers quote 99th for sizing)
   - Burst tolerance: how long do spikes last (seconds/minutes/hours)
4) Budget target (billable $/1M tokens) or a monthly spend target range we should aim for

Practical notes: for hosted pricing we’ll show a) a consumption-first band (no commit) and b) a discounted reserved band (3–12mo commit) with explicit burst capacity and 99th TPS SLO guidance. For the unit-econ exercise we’ll also need the percent of calls that are embeddings vs generation (if applicable) and whether you expect session affinity (long-lived KV cache) — both change cost materially.

I attached a tiny traffic sample template (traffic-sample-agg.csv) you can populate if it’s easier than answering the bullets directly. Also attaching a one-page MAP template you can scan and edit.

Next steps: if you can reply with the numbers above by EOD Wednesday (2 Jun), I’ll send back two sketch price bands + an operations note on expected latency at the 99th and recommended throttle settings.

Thanks —
Naomi Feldman
Sr. Account Exec, Redwood Inference
naomi@redwood.inference | +1 (415) 555-0126

Hi Naomi — thanks for the clean recap. Below are our best current estimates (we’ll validate with eng tomorrow and update if anything changes):

Monthly tokens
- Pilot (month 1): ~8.4M tokens
- Month 6 steady-state: 72M tokens/month (range 60–90M)

Token mix (averages)
- Input tokens (average per call): 95
- Output tokens (average per call): 210
- So total ~305 tokens per API call on average

Traffic shape / peak
- Typical day: 1.2M calls/day (averaged)
- Peak hour: ~90k calls/hour 
- That translates to peak TPS ~25 (sustained) and 99th percentile short bursts up to ~120 TPS (these last 30–90s occasionally during business events)

Embeddings: ~5% of calls (search index recalcs once every 24h)
Session affinity: yes — we expect to benefit from KV cache because many follow-ups are session-based; about 40% of calls are within an active session window.

Budget target
- Team-level guideline: $40k–$65k/month for the steady state (this includes any reserved capacity + margin for burst). If you can show a $/1M token equivalent that hits ~$45–$55/1M tokens we’ll be in the right ballpark.

I’ve attached a quick extract from our usage logs (traffic-sample-agg.csv) — it’s anonymized. Let me know if you need percentiles by minute rather than hour.

Thanks —
Ethan Brooks
Head of Platform, ClearHeath
ethan@clearheath.ai

Great — this is exactly the level of detail we need, thanks. Quick interpretation and two scenarios (back-of-envelope):

Assumptions from your numbers:
- Steady-state tokens: 72M/month
- Avg tokens per call: 305 -> implied calls/month ~236k
- Peak short-burst (99th): ~120 TPS for 30–90s
- Embeddings 5% (we will size embedding workers separately)

Scenario A — Consumption-first (no commit)
- Unit price we’d show: $65 / 1M tokens (baseline)
- Estimated monthly bill: 72 * $65 = $4,680 (note: this is illustrative; Redwood bills per 1M tokens rounding at invoice)
- Ops note: for 99th bursts to 120 TPS we recommend a small burst pool and a 95th/99th percentile routing policy; latency at 99th expected ~600–900ms for your model class on hosted endpoints.

Scenario B — Reserved/discounted (3–12mo commit)
- Unit price we’d preview for a 6mo commit: $45 / 1M tokens (with negotiated burst credit)
- Estimated monthly bill under commitment: 72 * $45 = $3,240
- Additional: dedicated reserved pool can lower 99th latency and provide predictable throughput; add-on for higher burst cushion (~ +$800/mo)

A few clarifying asks before we finalize the sketch:
- Can you confirm if the 72M tokens/month expectation includes any bulk document ingestion (one-time indexing) or is purely per-user traffic?
- Is the $40k–$65k/month budget inclusive of egress/networking costs your team wants to keep within the number? (we usually exclude heavy egress in the raw unit price unless requested)

I’m uploading a one-pager that maps these two scenarios into a simple MAP with proposed milestones. If everything looks reasonable we can convert Scenario B into a formal term sheet and hand to Legal/Procurement.

Next steps:
- Ethan, can you confirm the two clarifying points above?
- Assuming yes, we’ll circulate a MAP and a 6mo reserved sketch by EOD Thursday.

Thanks —
Naomi

Ethan — quick hello from me. Two operational notes from an infra sizing perspective before we lock things in:

1) Burst sizing: we can cover 120 TPS bursts for short windows without a Dedicated pool using autoscale and burst credits, but if you expect >120 TPS for multi-minute windows we should talk Reserved/Dedicated capacity.
2) KV/session cache: since ~40% of calls are session-based, enabling prefix/KV caching will likely reduce token compute by *reducing repeated context serialization* and cut cost ~10–18% depending on session lengths. We’ll add that to the MAP ops checklist.

I’ll work with Naomi to include an ops appendix in the MAP that lists throttle recommendations and a lightweight SLO table (99th latency, availability targets).

If the budget target of $40k–$65k/month is firm, the 6mo reserved scenario ($45/1M) should be achievable with a short contract and a small burst add-on.

Talk soon —
Karthik Iyer
Director, Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.inference
